subject: Actionable recap — p95/p99 latency targets and streaming constraints (hosted vs incumbent)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aria Li <aria@veridian.ai>; Veridian Platform <infra@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: p95/p99 targets, streaming constraints, and next actions

Thanks everyone for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a single place to land actions and acceptance criteria from the performance discussion. High-level notes and asks below.

Summary from the call:
- Veridian’s target: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms for their RAG/QA feature at current traffic mix (50% short prompts < 64 tokens, 30% medium 65-256, 20% long >256).
- Current provider meets p95 for short/medium but shows p99 spikes during concurrency peaks (notably when concurrency > 120).
- Streaming is required for live UI; client expects first token <= 60ms for short prompts and stable streaming throughput for long responses.

Key technical constraints we discussed:
1) Concurrency envelope: baseline 80 QPS sustained, burst to 200 QPS for 10-15s during peak events.
2) Throughput profile: median tokens per response ~ 120 tokens; long tails up to 1,200 tokens for summarization flows.
3) Network path: Veridian will share egress/path traces and NAT/per-region routing to help reproduce p99 events.

Immediate asks (action items):
- Veridian (Aria): share a 24-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized), and two example traces around p99 incidents (by 2027-06-13 EOD).
- Camila/Infra: run a lightweight hosted vs incumbent shadow test with a scripted 30-minute traffic window (80->200 QPS ramp) — Redwood to propose a test harness and time windows (I propose Wed 2027-06-16 09:00-09:45 PT).
- Ben/Irene: prepare the perf_matrix_v3.xlsx with mapping: request type, expected seq len, success criteria (p95/p99), and fallback model mapping (due 2027-06-14).
- Both parties: confirm whether KV cache prefixing is enabled in the Veridian path for RAG (affects early-token latency).

Notes on measurement and comparability:
- We will use end-to-end timing (client->app->Redwood/Incumbent->client) and align on clock sync methods. Please include any proxy timeouts, retries, and sample error logs when sharing traces.
- For streaming: first-byte latency and inter-token pacing are both acceptance metrics — propose first-byte p95 <= 60ms, p99 <= 160ms for short prompts as a starting point.

Attachments: perf_matrix_v3.xlsx (blank matrix attached), redwood-hosted-slo-proposal.pdf (proposal for target buckets and suggested fallback policies).

Next steps: please confirm the test window and deliverables above. If Wed 6/16 doesn't work, propose two alternate 45-minute windows.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Aria Li <aria@veridian.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Veridian Platform <infra@veridian.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 targets, streaming constraints, and next actions

Camila — thanks for the tight recap. Quick confirmation and clarifications below: 

1) We can provide a 24-hour anonymized traffic sample and two p99 incident traces by EOD 6/13. We'll scrub personal data and include per-request metadata (seq len, model id, start/end timestamps).
2) We currently have KV cache enabled for ~40% of queries (RAG prefetching). We'll provide config snapshot.
3) Test window: we prefer Thu 6/17 10:00-10:45 PT to avoid a deployment we have Wed morning. Can Redwood do that?

Also — two asks from our infra lead (cc'd):
- Can Redwood run the hosted shadow test from a us-west region and ensure source IPs are consistent (we want to filter traffic on our side)?
- For the shadow test, can you expose both streaming and non-streaming endpoints so we can compare first-byte vs whole-response latencies?

I'll upload the traces and a short description to the Drive link you suggested.

—Aria
VP, Product — Veridian

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aria Li <aria@veridian.ai>; Veridian Platform <infra@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 targets, streaming constraints, and next actions

Aria — Thu 6/17 10:00-10:45 PT works for Redwood. Confirming we will: 
- Stand up a shadow runner in us-west (single region) and run the scripted ramp (80 sustained, short bursts to 200 QPS).
- Expose both /v1/generate (non-stream) and /v1/stream endpoints, and include request/response IDs in logs for trace correlation.
- Provide a short smoke script (Python) and the harness (k6 + wrapper) so Veridian can replay locally if desired.

Ben/Irene — Ben, can you lead the test execution and coordinate the smoke script handoff to Veridian infra? Irene, please attach the perf_matrix_v3 with initial thresholds (I put placeholders in tab "Acceptance").

If we see p99 regressions on hosted, we'll run simultaneous sampling against the incumbent to compare tail source (model compute vs network). Also we'll capture per-node latency and kernel-level counters (where available) to help isolate causes.

Deliverables & owners: 
- perf_matrix_v3.xlsx — Ben/Irene (due 6/14)
- Shadow test harness + k6 script — Camila/Redwood infra (deliver 6/15 morning PT)
- Veridian traces & scrubbed traffic sample — Veridian (deliver 6/13 EOD)
- Post-test results and preliminary report — Redwood (deliver 6/18 EOD)

Thanks — I'll calendar the 6/17 window and send dial-in + runbook.

Camila

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Aria Li <aria@veridian.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 targets, streaming constraints, and next actions

Quick update — attached perf_matrix_v3.xlsx has initial acceptance buckets. Irene added notes on fallback models and suggested quantization/parallelism knobs to try if we see p99 regressions with longer sequences.

Irene — can you also add a short checklist for what we want Veridian to capture in the traces (timestamps at ingress/egress, proxy durations, retry counts)? I'll incorporate that into the runbook.

Aria — thanks for shifting to 6/17. We'll confirm runbook and share the k6 harness by 6/15 morning PT. Looking forward to the shadow run.

—Ben
